sentences.text: These two Criminal Miscellaneous cases are connected and therefore, I am disposing of these cases by a common order because same point is raised in these cases.
I will narrate the facts in Crl.M.C.No. 6319/2017.
2. Petitioner is the 2nd accused in S.T.No.1030/2016 on the file of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court - II, Kothamangalam.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court - II, Kothamangalam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The above case is registered alleging offences punishable under the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

On 18.02.2015 at about 3.45 p.m., the 1 st respondent, Food Safety Officer of Kothamangalam Circle visited Crl.M.C. Nos.6319 of 2017 & 2464 of 2018 2024:KER:65531 the warehouse of M/s. Eastern Chai (Pvt) Ltd. and in the store room of the company 1000 kg of tea dust was seen packed in 250 grams each sealed and labeled packets and from the said stock 8 packets of 250 grams each tea dust was taken as sample by the 1 st respondent.

From those 8 packets, two packets each, were tied together, and four sample units were prepared by the 1st respondent and from such sample units, one sample unit was sent for chemical analysis to the Regional Analytical Laboratory, Ernakulam and a report was received and based on the same,
Annexure-I complaint was filed.
Annexure-II is the food analyst report in Form B.
As per Annexure-II, the tea dust contains iron filings which is quantified at 592.25 mg/Kg and as per the report, iron filing shall be absent.

Being aggrieved by the opinion expressed by the food analyst in Annexure-II report, another part Crl.M.C. Nos.6319 of 2017 & 2464 of 2018 2024:KER:65531 of the sample was sent on the request of the petitioner to the Referral Laboratory, Kolkotta and a report in Form A was received as evident by Annexure-III.
In column No.8 of Annexure-III report, it is stated that iron filings detected at 1378.39 mg/Kg.
As per the report, iron filings shall be absent.
Hence it is alleged that the accused committed the offence.
3. Crl.M.C. No.2464/2018 is filed to quash the proceedings in S.T. No. 1534/2017 on the file of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court - III, Kottayam.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court - III, Kottayam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In this case also, the prosecution is as per the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
It is stated that the tea dust seized as per Annexure-II was sent for analysis, and the analyst reported that there is iron filing.
Hence it is alleged that the accused committed the offence.
According to the petitioners, even if the entire allegations are accepted, no offence Crl.M.C. Nos.6319 of 2017 & 2464 of 2018 2024:KER:65531 is made out.
Hence these Criminal Miscellaneous Cases are filed.

4. Heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners and the learned Additional Director General of Prosecution.
5.
The short point raised by the petitioners is that, in the light of the order dated 17.08.2023 in Crl.M.C. No.7955/2017, the prosecution against the petitioners is to be quashed.
I think there is force in the above contention.

The sample of tea dust in S.T.No. 1534/2017 on the file of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court - III, Kottayam was taken on 04.02.2016 and the sample of tea dust in S.T. No.1030/2016 on the file of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court - II, Kothamangalam was Muhammed Sabir vs Food Safety Officer on 23 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149350961/
3 taken on 18.02.2015.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It will be beneficial to extract the order dated 17.08.2023 in Crl.M.C.
No.7955/2017:
"The petitioner herein is the 2nd accused in Crl.M.C. Nos.6319 of 2017 & 2464 of 2018 2024:KER:65531 S.T.No. 831 of 2016 on the file of the Judicial First Class Magistrate-I, Idukki.

In the aforesaid case, he is facing prosecution for having committed offences punishable under Section3.1 (zz) (iii) & (xi), 26 2(i), 27(i) and 59(i) of FSS Act, 2006 r/w. Regulation No. 2.10.1:(1) of Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standard and Food Additives) Regulations 2011.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standard and Food Additives) Regulations 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. The prosecution alleges that on 12.02.2016, at approximately 3.30 PM, an inspection was conducted at Door No.III/165-A shop namely Sneha Agencies of Idukki-Kanjikuzhy Grama Panchayath, and 2 kg of tea were seized for analysis by the food analyst.
The samples were analyzed by the Food Analyst of the Regional Analytical Laboratory, Kakkanad.

As per the report, the sample contains extraneous matter (iron filings) to the extent of not less than 191.35 mg per kg, which is in excess of the safe limit, and hence the food was categorised as unsafe.

3. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submitted that the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, through its Director (RCD) had issued Annexure- IV order dated 02.11.2017, whereby directions were issued to the States not to launch prosecution for non-conformance of the limit of iron filings for cases where samples were picked up/tested prior to 19.05.2016.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Directions were Crl.M.C. Nos.6319 of 2017 & 2464 of 2018 2024:KER:65531 also issued to withdraw all such prosecutions launched prior to 19.05.2016, either under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 or under the PFA Act, 1954.

The learned counsel submits that in identical circumstances, this Court had quashed the proceedings against the accused by order dated 05.02.2018 in Crl.
M.C.No.3248 of 2017.
4. The learned Public Prosecutor has opposed the submissions.

He points out that even as of date,
the upper limit of iron filings permitted in tea has not been finalized by the Food Safety Authority.
5. I have considered the submissions advanced.
The order dated 02.11.2017 is seen issued by the Director.

Paragraph No. 5 of the order reads as under:-
"The matter has been examined in FSSAI.
It is felt that till a reliable method of assessment/testing of iron filings in Tea is finalised.

It would not be appropriate to launch prosecution non- conformance nor is it proper to pursue or continue with the prosecutions launched under PFA Act/FSS Act prior to issue of FSSAI's Order dated 19.05.2016.

Commissioners of Food Safety, All states/UTs are, therefore, directed not to launch prosecutions for non-conformance of limit of iron filings for cases where samples were picked up/tested prior to 19.05.2016.

They are also advised to Muhammed Sabir vs Food Safety Officer on 23 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149350961/
4 withdraw all such prosecutions Crl.M.C. Nos.6319 of 2017 & 2464 of 2018 2024:KER:65531 launched prior to 19.05.2016 either under FSS Act, 2006 or PFA Act, 1954."
6.

entities.text: Muhammed Sabir vs Food Safety Officer
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant case, the sample was taken on 07.12.2015 and therefore, the petitioner is entitled to the benefits of the above order.
This petition will stand allowed.
All further proceedings against the petitioner in S.T. No. 831/2016 Of Judicial Magistrate Of First Class -I, Idukki, are quashed."

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate Of First Class -I, Idukki
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 6. From the above, it is clear that no prosecution can be initiated for cases where the samples were picked up/tested prior to 19.05.2016.
Admittedly, in these cases, the samples were picked up/tested prior to 19.05.2016.
If that be the case, the prosecution is unsustainable.

Therefore, these Criminal Miscellaneous Cases are allowed in the following manner:
1.

In Crl.M.C. No.2464/2018, all further proceedings against the petitioner in S.T.
No.1534/2017 on the file of the Judicial First Crl.M.C. Nos.6319 of 2017 & 2464 of 2018 2024:KER:65531 Class Magistrate Court - III, Kottayam are quashed.
